The world should feel active, inhabited and larger than the visible frame, with layered depth, while the composition stays clear. Overall: lived-in, cyber, illustrated science fiction, lit and readable: warm lamplight against cool blue-steel shadow, dark only in the corners. This is a still picture and code adds the motion, so paint everything crisply: no motion blur, no lens blur, no film grain.

Room A, the crew bay, in the same illustrated world: blue steel, lit warm. The whole room is one blue-steel family, the colours of the attached guide: deep navy in the shadows and corners (#14243F, #1D3D6B), steel blue on the walls and the deck (#2D609E), turning paler where the light falls (#5C92CC, #A9CAEB). The light is warm: the two light bars glow cream along their length (#FCE3A0), with a warm paper-white glow (#F4EBDD) on the ceiling around them and soft pools of pale light on the deck below. Walls, panels, pipes, cables and deck plates take their colour from that family; worn edges, rivets and plate seams show a little rust (#75402E); nothing is neutral grey, and nothing is tan, beige, olive, purple or violet. The shadows are deep navy, never black-brown or grey. Labels and paper are blank, in a warm paper white (#F4EBDD). Practical and worn, a working bay, quiet but lived in. The guide is the room's colour plan: paint over it in full detail and texture, but keep its colours and where its light falls.

The room: Room A, the crew bay, a 4 m square room with a 3 m ceiling, here with no furniture in it. The ceiling is solid steel panels, with no skylight and no opening in it: two long light bars set into it run across the room about 1.4 m apart, each glowing warm cream along its whole length behind a plain diffuser, lighting the ceiling around it and throwing soft pools of light on the deck below. In the middle of the north wall, about 1.95 m above the deck, a round window about 1 m across sits in a heavy steel frame; its glass is flat black and empty, with nothing seen through it. The walls are steel panels, pipes, conduits, cable runs and small lockers, worn and repaired, darker toward the deck, with a narrow rust-brown kick strip along their foot; the deck is metal plates with seams, scuffs and a little rust, lit pale under the light bars and darker toward the corners. No beams, rays or shafts of light in the air.

The horizon, at eye level, is a straight line 714 px from the top, a little above the middle. Match the guide's layout, perspective, horizon and proportions exactly, line for line, as its floor seams, wall bases, corners and ceiling edges show. Do not curve the lines, tilt the view, zoom in or out, or move the horizon.

Ahead, the north wall, from its corner with the west wall a little left of the middle out to the right edge, with the round window right of the middle; on the left, the west wall. The deck is open and clear, with nothing standing on it, while the walls keep their pipes, panels and conduits.
